expected.summary: Ten minutes before the anchor the data-science team's CronJob ml-feature-backfill started two pods, ml-feature-backfill-28817-x2kq and ml-feature-backfill-28817-p7wd, which the scheduler placed on nodes ip-10-0-5-21 and ip-10-0-5-88, the nodes that host search-1 and search-4. They request 500m of CPU and have no CPU limit, so they take most of those nodes' CPU. Over two minutes search-1 and search-4 slowed on their own work: their server spans grew from about 20 ms to 400 ms or more and they logged event loop delay and cpu steal of 35 to 50 percent on their nodes, while their es.search spans and the other four search pods stayed normal. Requests that land on those two pods often take longer than the BFFs' 500 ms timeout, so about one GET /search in eight fails with 504, all of them on search-1 and search-4, and the failures propagate through web-bff and mobile-bff to edge-gateway, where the alert fires. Every other route is healthy. Elasticsearch is healthy and search's version did not change. The catalog rollout from 1.4.2 to 1.4.3, six minutes before the failures, is unrelated: catalog serves no errors and search's calls to it stay fast.
contributingFactors: the data-science CronJob ml-feature-backfill scheduled with no CPU limit onto the nodes hosting search-1 and search-4
the BFFs' 500 ms timeout on search

criteria.description: Does the brief place the origin at search-1 and search-4, slowed by another team's CronJob (ml-feature-backfill) taking the CPU of the nodes they run on, with their requests outlasting the BFFs' timeout and the failures reaching edge-gateway? 5 = the co-scheduled job, the two pods and nodes, and the timeout path. Saying only that search is slow scores at most 2.

Is it grounded in the failures concentrating on two pods, those pods' own time rising while es.search stays fast, the cpu steal warnings and the scheduling lines naming ml-feature-backfill? Cap at 3 unless it names the job or the nodes.
Does it avoid blaming Elasticsearch, the catalog 1.4.3 rollout, a traffic surge, a search deploy or edge-gateway?
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
